Class Robot

java.lang.Object
Robot
public class Robot extends Object
A Robot is a simple, self-contained object (inspired by Richard Pattis' "Karel the Robot") that lives on a grid of cells, can move in one of four directions (N, S, E, W) and can move forward/backward along the direction it is looking at. VISUAL DESIGN: Assembled using shapes from the "shapes" package: - 1 Triangle (Black Head) - 1 Circle (Blue Body) - 1 Circle (Red Eye / direction indicator) - 2 Rectangles (Black Arms) - 1 Rectangle (Red "dead face" mark, Part III extension — shown instead of the eye once die() is called; see below) DESIGN (matches the UML diagram strictly): Cycle 1 -> constructor + attributes: coordinates, direction Cycle 2 -> move(step), turn(direction), coordinates() Cycle 3 -> makeVisible(), makeInvisible(), isOK()
Version:
1.1
Author:
Oscar Poveda, Elian Ibarra

    • die

      public void die()
      Part III (RobotMaze) extension — not part of the original Part II-A UML diagram. Changes the robot's on-canvas appearance once it runs out of lives, and that appearance is made up of this class's private shapes, so the change has to live here. Calling this swaps the red eye for a flat red "dead face" mark. Called automatically by loseLife() once life reaches 0. Idempotent: calling it more than once has no further effect.

    • getLife

      public int getLife()
      Returns:
      the robot's remaining life points.

    • loseLife

      public void loseLife()
      Part III (RobotMaze) extension. Makes the robot lose one life point (e.g. after colliding with a wall or the maze border). When life reaches 0, the robot automatically dies (see die()). Has no further effect once life is already at 0.
